title: In tests, select a pre-existing experiment by resolving its ID instead of by name
answers: evaluation run logged to Default experiment instead of the test experiment
mlflow set_experiment recreated experiment with ./mlruns fallback
compatibility test experiment not found after 2.x migration
how to activate an existing experiment in a test
body:
Symptom: In the 2.x-to-3.x compatibility test, the evaluation run is logged to the Default experiment rather than the experiment the 2.x run created.
Root cause: mlflow.set_experiment(name) creates the experiment when no experiment with that name exists, and the recreated experiment falls back to the ./mlruns artifact location.
Fix pattern: Resolve the existing experiment with mlflow.get_experiment_by_name, assert it is not None so a missing experiment fails loudly, then call mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_id=experiment.experiment_id).
Constraints: Use this when the test expects the experiment to already exist. Setting by name is fine when creating the experiment is intended.
applies: Test code in tests/test_mlflow_version_comp.py and similar cross-version tests that reopen an earlier-created tracking store.
says: After upgrading versions, evaluation runs are being recorded under the default experiment instead.
Migrated experiments disappear and evaluation results fall back to the default artifact location.
Upgrading releases causes existing tracking experiments to be recreated rather than reused.
Ensure version upgrades preserve existing experiment associations instead of creating duplicate default experiments.
Compatibility checks log evaluation runs into the wrong experiment after migrating earlier tracking data.
search: In cross-version compatibility tests reopening existing tracking stores, pre-existing experiments must be selected by resolving experiment_id rather than by name. Calling mlflow.set_experiment by name recreates missing experiments with a fallback ./mlruns artifact location, causing evaluation runs in test_mlflow_2_x_comp to log under the Default experiment. Tests must resolve the experiment using mlflow.get_experiment_by_name, assert it is not None to catch missing experiments loudly, and call mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_id=experiment.experiment_id). This constraint applies specifically to tests expecting an already created experiment in tests/test_mlflow_version_comp.py, while setting by name remains valid when intentionally creating an experiment.
